node.title: Re^2: Please Help! This is a class assignment given to me.
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Every perl program starts with the same three lines of code. And this is just to get you started: #!/usr/bin/perl -w use strict; use warnings;

Both [doc://warnings|use warnings] and [doc://perlrun#*-w*|-w] isn't needed, see: [doc://warnings#What's-wrong-with-*-w*-and-$^W|What's wrong with -w and $^W]

Personally I prefer the shebang #!/usr/bin/env perl to say "use whatever perl is in my PATH" (see [man://env]), it'll also work better with e.g. [https://perlbrew.pl/|perlbrew]. Pointing to a specific perl binary makes sense if distributing a script to a system where you may not have control over the PATH (e.g. CGI scripts on hosting providers).

Update: I agree with [Tux]'s reply: In the case of the shebang, TIMTOWTDI.
